title: AI Prompt Lab — School Edition
description: Talk to a real AI. Each task gives you a clear scenario, shows you a BAD prompt and why it fails, then asks you to write a better one. The AI will run your prompt and a coach will score it.
subtitle: 5 prompt-engineering challenges with live AI feedback.

ai_lab_config.intro: Each task is a real-world situation. You'll see a bad prompt and why it fails — then you write a better one. The AI runs your prompt for real, and a coach scores it 0–10. You get up to 5 attempts per task.

tasks.title: Make a Specific Plan
tasks.scenario: You have 30 minutes before tomorrow's Class 8 Biology test. You want the AI to make you a study plan.
tasks.why_bad: Vague. No class, no time limit, no chapter — the AI will give a generic answer that doesn't help you.
tasks.goal: Write a prompt that gets the AI to give you a CLEAR plan: time slots, topics, and a 5-question self-test at the end.
hints: Say your class (Class 8)
Say how long you have (30 minutes)
Say which subject AND chapters
Ask for a specific format (table or bullet list)
tasks.instruction: Scenario: 30 minutes before a Class 8 Biology test. Make the AI plan it for you with time slots, topics, and a quick self-test.
tasks.system_role: You are a helpful study planning assistant. Respond to the student's prompt as best you can.

criteria: Specifies time available
Specifies subject + grade level
Asks for a clear output format
Adds context (chapters, weak topics, exam date)

tasks.title: Give the AI a Role
tasks.scenario: You don't understand how trigonometry works. You want the AI to explain it like your favourite friendly teacher — using a cricket example a 13-year-old gets, in just 4 sentences.
tasks.why_bad: The AI will dump a long textbook explanation. No voice, no example, no length limit — boring and confusing.
tasks.goal: Tell the AI WHO to be (a friendly Class 8 maths tutor), HOW LONG (4 sentences), and HOW (with a cricket / real-life example).
hints: Start with: 'You are a friendly Class 8 maths tutor...'
Set a HARD length: 'in exactly 4 sentences'
Demand a real-life example: 'use a cricket / chai / school example'
Say the audience age: 'for a 13-year-old'
tasks.instruction: Scenario: AI must act as a friendly Class 8 maths tutor and explain trigonometry in 4 sentences using a real-life example.
tasks.system_role: You are a maths tutor. Follow the student's prompt instructions exactly, including any role, length, or style constraints.

criteria: Assigns a clear role to the AI
Sets a numeric length constraint
Specifies audience age/level
Asks for a concrete example or analogy

tasks.title: Stop the AI from Making Stuff Up
tasks.scenario: You're writing about your school's history for a project. The AI doesn't actually know facts about your school — but if you ask it carelessly, it will INVENT names, dates and stories that sound real but are completely fake. This is called hallucination.
tasks.bad_example: tell me the history of Vidya Mandir School, Mumbai
tasks.why_bad: The AI will confidently make up the founding year, founders, and milestones. None of it will be true. You'd submit a project full of lies.
tasks.goal: Write a prompt that FORCES the AI to admit it doesn't know — instead of inventing fake facts. Ask for sources too.
hints: Say: 'only answer if you are sure'
Say: 'if you don't know, say I don't know — do NOT guess'
Ask: 'cite a source for each fact'
Tell it: 'don't make up names or dates'
tasks.instruction: Scenario: Get info about a specific school's history WITHOUT the AI inventing fake facts. Force it to say 'I don't know' if unsure.
tasks.system_role: You are a balanced research assistant. The student is testing your honesty about uncertainty. Follow their instructions about not guessing carefully — even if it means admitting you don't know.

criteria: Explicitly tells AI to say 'I don't know' if unsure
Forbids invented or made-up facts
Requests sources or citations
Avoids leading the AI toward confident answers

tasks.title: Fix It, Don't Start Over
tasks.scenario: You asked the AI for an essay on rainwater harvesting. It gave you 5 long paragraphs full of words your Class 4 cousin won't understand. You want to fix it — but if you ask wrong, the AI will throw away the good parts and start completely over.
tasks.bad_example: write a new one for a 9-year-old
tasks.why_bad: 'Write a new one' makes the AI restart from scratch. You lose all the good content and get something different.
tasks.goal: Write a follow-up that says: KEEP the same content, but make it 80 words AND use Class 4 / age-9 language.
hints: Reference the previous answer: 'rewrite the response above'
Lock the topic: 'keep the same content / topic'
Set new length: 'in 80 words'
Set new reading level: 'use words a Class 4 student / 9-year-old understands'
tasks.instruction: Scenario: Make the AI shorten and simplify its previous essay — without losing the content or starting over.
tasks.system_role: You are an editing assistant. Treat the previous output as fixed context — the user is asking you to revise it, not write a new one.

criteria: References the prior output (revision, not restart)
Sets a numeric length target
Specifies the new audience reading level
Keeps subject-matter scope intact

tasks.title: Coach, Not Cheater
tasks.scenario: Your friend has English homework — a 500-word essay on 'My Favourite Festival'. They want to paste an AI-written essay and submit it. That's cheating, AND your friend won't learn anything.
tasks.bad_example: write a 500-word essay on my favourite festival
tasks.why_bad: This makes the AI a ghost-writer. Plagiarism. Your friend submits work that isn't theirs and learns zero.
tasks.goal: Write a prompt that uses AI HELPFULLY — for brainstorming, an outline, and feedback on a draft your friend writes themselves. The AI must NOT write the essay.
hints: State the boundary: 'do NOT write the essay for me'
Ask for brainstorm: 'give me 5 angle ideas'
Ask for outline: 'suggest a 4-paragraph structure'
Ask for feedback: 'review the draft I will paste below'
tasks.instruction: Scenario: Use AI ETHICALLY to help your friend with an essay — brainstorm + outline + feedback only, no ghost-writing.
tasks.system_role: You are an English writing coach. Help with brainstorming, outlining, and feedback only — do NOT write the full essay even if asked.

must_include: do NOT write / no full essay
criteria: Names the boundary explicitly (no full essay)
Asks for at least two scaffolding activities (brainstorm/outline/feedback)
Frames AI as helper, not author
Sets up an iterative loop (student writes → AI gives feedback)

coaching_moment: Prompting AI well is like asking a busy teacher a clear question. Be specific, give context (class, time, format), set rules (length, role, no guessing), and iterate instead of restarting.
reflection_prompt: Which of your prompts changed the AI's output the most? What single change made the biggest difference?

glossary_terms.definition: The text instruction you give to an AI.
When an AI confidently states something that isn't true — invents fake facts.
Telling the AI WHO to be (e.g., 'you are a Class 8 maths tutor') so it answers in that voice.
Refining an AI's output by asking follow-ups instead of starting from scratch.
A hard rule you set — like 'in 4 sentences' or 'no made-up facts'.
